h: Castles, rivers and a sneaky slope
p: Tonbridge sits in a cracking spot for history lovers. Penshurst Place, a medieval manor house with famous walled gardens, is only a few miles away, and Hever Castle near Edenbridge, the childhood home of Anne Boleyn, is a short drive too. Hever is especially good for families, with its maze and lakeside grounds. Combine either with a round of crazy golf back in town and you've covered both ends of the fun spectrum: Tudor romance and terrible putting.

Closer to home, Haysden Country Park on the western edge of Tonbridge has lakes, woodland paths and plenty of space for kids to let off steam, and it's a lovely free option if the sun comes out after your game. The River Medway is also popular for boating in the warmer months.

As for the golf, allow roughly an hour for a round. If you've got a group of more than six, it's worth splitting into two teams so the pace doesn't drag and nobody ends up waiting ages for their turn. Let the kids go first, keep the scorecard honest, and save the trash talk for the final hole.

Tonbridge also has quick rail links into London, so it's easy to reach without a car, and the station is within walking distance of the town centre. With the castle, the river and the High Street all close by, you can easily make a relaxed day of it without much travelling at all.
